SMTO-HTTP-0064 — The web request's content was set up the wrong way

GUID: 7463e59e-0f43-468f-b6ca-d55e01138530
Slug: http-body-mode-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The request tried to send content in more than one form at once, sent content with a read-only request, or had content SMTO couldn't package. SMTO didn't send it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the request only reads data, ask the Agent to send it without any content and put search values in the web address instead. Reading actions like GET can't carry content, so SMTO refuses to send one that does.
  2. If the request sends data, ask the Agent to send it in just one form, the one the service's documentation shows, using POST, PUT or PATCH. Mixing forms leaves it unclear what should be sent, so SMTO accepts exactly one.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with what you wanted the request to do.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The request body was rejected: more than one of json_body, text_body, form_body, multipart_body or body_reference was supplied, a body was sent with a read method (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS), a text or form value was invalid, or body encoding failed.

What this means

  • More than one body mode is supplied, a read-class method includes a body, form/text values are invalid, or body serialization fails. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • More than one body mode is supplied, a read-class method includes a body, form/text values are invalid, or body serialization fails.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the selected method and one body representation with the endpoint contract and safe serialization error.

How to fix it

  • Supply exactly one body field and use it only with a write method (POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE). Pass JSON objects as json_body objects rather than serialized JSON strings, keep form_body values scalar, and use text_body only for strings.
  • Choose exactly one supported body representation with POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Keep objects as objects rather than serialized JSON strings.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Exactly one valid body mode is encoded for a supported write-class method.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
